newsitem.title: GERMANY: German computer industry sees further 97 growth.
newsitem.headline: German computer industry sees further 97 growth.

text.p: The German computer industry expects robust growth again this year after strong expansion in 1996, an industry association said on Thursday.

The industry posted five percent growth in service, hardware and software turnover for 1996 to 80.5 billion marks, and foresees another six percent climb for the current year, said the chairman of the German computer industry association, Joerg Menno Harms.
Harms said he expected double-digit expansion in the computer service sector to help propel growth for the industry in 1997.

"Computer services are developing into a real growth engine," Harms said. "Computer centre services and network services now make up a fifth of the entire information technology market with volume of 17 billion marks."
Turnover in the current year is expected to reach 85.6 billion marks, and the industry's sales should surpass 100 billion marks by the year 2000, Harms said.
Harms said the introduction of a single currency in Europe in 1999 and the problem of the "Millenium Bug" would also drive demand for hiring in the industry.

The Millenium Bug is a worldwide programming problem that will cause many computers to view the year 2000 as the year 1900. It has been called the largest problem ever to face the information technology industry.
Until then, German consumers can at least expect a dip in prices of between three and five percent before the year 2000, largely due to lower customs duties, Harms added.

The German computer industry association is part of the Association of German Machinery and Construction (VDMA) and the Central Association of Electrical Engineering and the Electronics Industry (ZVEI).
